subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

must_contain: A marked one-dimensional axis with a declared positive direction.
An out-and-back path where path length is nonzero but the finish is at the start.

controlled_variation.vary: how far the traveller goes before returning to the start
controlled_variation.hold: the same start and finish point
controlled_variation.notice: distance changes while displacement remains zero

controlled_variation.vary: the finish point on the marked axis
controlled_variation.notice: equal distances can end with different signed displacements

must_contain: A round trip with unequal speeds on equal-distance legs.
The total-distance-over-total-time construction written before any averaging shortcut.

controlled_variation.hold: equal distance on both legs and the faster leg's speed
controlled_variation.notice: the slower leg occupies more of the total time and pulls the average speed toward it

must_contain: A velocity-time plot crossing zero with a nonzero slope.
The instant at the top of a vertical trip distinguished from an interval of rest.

controlled_variation.vary: the instant from just before to just after the top of the motion
controlled_variation.notice: velocity passes through zero and changes sign while acceleration keeps the same direction
the time of the zero-velocity instant changes but the acceleration at that instant does not

must_contain: A position-time graph with labelled time and position axes and at least two plotted points.
A velocity-time graph with labelled time and velocity axes and at least two plotted points.
An explicit distinction between graph height and graph slope.

controlled_variation.vary: the vertical-axis quantity from position to velocity
controlled_variation.hold: the same time axis and interval-reading procedure
controlled_variation.notice: segment slope changes meaning from average velocity to average acceleration

controlled_variation.vary: the segment from sloped to horizontal
controlled_variation.notice: the corresponding interval rate becomes zero when the numerator change is zero

must_contain: Two velocity-time plots over equal intervals, one straight and one curved.
A check of whether acceleration is constant before any constant-acceleration equation is selected.

controlled_variation.vary: the time interval chosen on a straight velocity-time graph
controlled_variation.notice: the same acceleration describes every sub-interval

controlled_variation.vary: the graph from straight to curved
controlled_variation.hold: the same starting velocity and total duration
controlled_variation.notice: one acceleration value no longer describes every part of the motion

must_contain: Equal-length tangent velocity arrows at different points on one circle.
An inward acceleration arrow distinguished from the tangent velocity direction.
A one-revolution path length 2 pi r divided by a positive revolution period T.

controlled_variation.hold: the same speed and circle radius
controlled_variation.notice: velocity direction changes while speed stays constant

controlled_variation.vary: the path from curved toward straight
controlled_variation.notice: the turning acceleration shrinks toward zero as direction stops changing

family.invariant_demand: Declare the positive direction and time interval, distinguish path quantities from signed change, choose a relation whose assumptions fit the motion, and keep velocity and acceleration as separate quantities.
family.difficult_move: Deciding from the words or graph which signed quantity and which motion model are actually being asked for before substituting numbers.
family.independent_check: The sign must match the declared axis, units must match the requested quantity, and any constant-acceleration calculation must agree with the slope/shape of the velocity-time representation.

support_ladder.handed_over: The positive direction, time interval, and the relevant motion representation are labelled.
The positive direction and time interval are labelled.
Only the story, table, path, or graph is supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A position-time or velocity-time graph segment must be translated into the correct interval-rate statement without a verbal motion story.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the segment slope represents average velocity or average acceleration

transfer.changed_demand: A motion interval has changing acceleration and the learner must decide that constant-acceleration equations are not an exact model.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether acceleration is constant over the interval

transfer.changed_demand: A journey reverses direction in several stages, requiring segment-by-segment distance, displacement, and elapsed-time accounting.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which segment signs contribute to displacement but not to distance

transfer.changed_demand: A constant speed is maintained on a curved path, requiring the learner to decide whether acceleration can still be nonzero.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether changing direction alone counts as a change of velocity

transfer.changed_demand: A complete circular revolution is described by radius and period, requiring the learner to construct circumference before computing the uniform speed.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that one revolution travels path length 2 pi r
